steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease 10 muffin cups or line with paper liners.

Combine 1 ½ cups flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Beat bananas, ⅓ cup melted butter, white sugar, and egg in separate bowl; stir into flour mixture just until moistened. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups.
Combine brown sugar, 2 tablespoons flour, and cinnamon in a small bowl; cut in 1 tablespoon butter with a fork until mixture resembles coarse cornmeal. Sprinkle over muffins.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden and tops spring back when lightly pressed, 18 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Banana Crumb Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This healthier banana crumb muffin recipe is healthier because of additional bananas and less sugar and uses only 10 ingredients to make 10 muffins.
raw_recipe.name: Healthier Banana Crumb Muffins

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe exact. I did bake my muffins at 350*, they were done in 20 minutes. I loved that this recipe used a minimal amount of sugar especially since my bananas were quite ripe and sweet enough on their own. My whole family loved these!

I took a healthier approach and made a few substitutions. Stevia in place of granulated sugar, gluten free potato-rice flour in place of reg flour, coconut oil in place of butter. I also added some freshly ground peanut butter (organic no sugar added) a tsp of peanut butter extract, cinnamon, vanilla extract and baked them in mini muffin tins :) came out super moist and flavorful. My daughter loves them!

This recipe is extremely similar to the original, even in exact appearance. The only change I see is an exta banana was used and the refined sugar is cut by a half a cup. I have to admit I actually like the base on these better as they taste more like banana than sugar. Although, I would like to rework the topping. I found it to sugary on the original recipe too. Both recipes also have a soft texture and for whatever reason I prefer a more dense muffin. Really liked how the refined sugar was adjusted on this without affecting the recipe though. I took them out of the oven at 18 minutes. The topping seemed pretty much done, while the batter on top appeared slightly wet looking still. I turned off the oven, but set them back in for about eight minutes, checking twice, and it worked. They were perfectly baked.

Recipe came out great. Made a few modifications: instead of using the brown sugar and cinnamon as a topping, I added it to the mixture. And replaced the 1/4 cup of sugar with a 1/2 of cup of sweetener (Splenda). I also left out the extra tablespoon of butter and 2 tablespoons of flour. I added to caps of vanilla extract and used slices of bananas as the topping instead. Cook time was about 15 mins. Great recipe! Thanks

So I tried to make it even healthier.. I ditched the crumb topping, replaced 1/3 melted butter with unsweetened applesauce, used whole wheat pastry flour instead of all purpose, and made mini muffins.. One recipe made 42 mini muffins.. Baked them for 13 minutes..... 32 calories a piece!! And DELISH!

Delicious and bursting with banana-ness! Made these for my toddler *crossing my fingers that she loves them* though I'll eat them if she doesn't. It's super simple. Cut the baking time to about 10 minutes (probably should have toothpick tested at 8....since they kept cooking as they cooled in the pan). Didn't need to grease in my nonstick and cut the sugar down to 1/4 cup - and that was plenty for my ripe bananas! Only used 3 bananas b/c that's what I had on hand....this is such a good recipe for 12+ month olds. Left off the streusel topping - I don't need her jumping off the walls before bedtime! Still plenty sweet.

Added 3T chia seeds, dark chocolate chips and walnuts. Subbed 1/2 C of the flour with almond flour, coconut oil for butter, flaxseed for egg and Demerara sugar. Also for topping, used nutmeg, cinnamon and monk fruit sugar for topping. Delish!!! Yes, adjusted recipe beyond recognition, but love that I could use up 4 ripe bananas!

So delicious! I did end up adding a tablespoon of cinnamon to the dry ingredients and some vanilla to the banana mixture as some reviewers suggested. These are so good! I couldn’t even wait for them to cool before tasting!

Fantastic recipe! I made a few minor changes, including subbing half of the butter for 1/3 C of pureed pumpkin that I had leftover in the fridge, adding 1 tsp. cinnamon to the batter, and adding some oats to the crumb topping. Baked at 350 for 20 minutes, made 12 muffins instead of 10. Will absolutely make again!

I found this to be a simple, healthy recipe for muffins. I always add/ substitute extra healthy stuff into my muffins, so instead of butter, I used olive oil. I added a 1/2 cup oats and 1/4 cup mini semi-sweet chocolate chips, as well as I used 2 eggs to up the protein quotient some. And, as I am that mom that adds wheat germ to "everything," I added 1/2 cup wheat germ (with cinnamon and flax.) These come out tasty, hearty, and a great way to use up almost dead bananas.
As I was going for healthy, and since I add the chocolate chips, I always skip out on adding the topping. I have made these numerous times....soooo good!

Oh my goodness! I’ve made a lot of banana bread in my day, my past favorite included sour cream. This recipe moves to the top of my go-to list from now on??. I did substitute applesauce for butter and truvia for the sugar only in the bread batter. Left the crumb topping as is and it was superior to any I’ve ever eaten. Thank you so much for sharing!
Thank you for sharing this recipe, moist and yummy! Looking forward to serving this to our grandchildren.
I was looking for a replacement recipe for banana bread which always seems so heavy. This is the answer! The muffins came out light and the topping was just the right amount of crisp.
Really good-love the streusel like topping! I will be making this again. I did have extra mix over the 10 muffins so I did a little loaf also.
Very good as written but also works very well with a cup of leftover cooked cranberries instead of the bananas.😁
So I just made this for my family, and it was great! My brother did say that it wasn’t very sweet though, but I didn’t notice it. Also, it makes 12 muffins if you fill them 3/4 of the way.

Very good! I only had three bananas so I added about 1/4 cup applesauce to make up for the missing banana. I added a little rolled oats to the topping. I like that only small amount of sugar is used and they came out moist and delicious. I will be making these again. Thank you!!

I have made this recipe twice now for my family. These muffins are a huge hit with everyone. Even my daughter who isn’t so keen on bananas. The only thing that I did different was add a little more cinnamon to the topping, as well as some old-fashioned oats. I love that the sugar level in these muffins is lower but they still have a wonderful flavor. I’m starting to think my family is purposely letting our bananas get too ripe so that I will make muffins out of them! Thanks for the recipe.
This recipe is good, I added some coconut flakes on a few of the muffin?s. Maybe next time I will add some walnuts. I will definitely make this recipe again.
